content.title: Peter Alexander exits NBC for rival role
content.text: A heartfelt farewell after 22 years Peter Alexander announced his departure from NBC News during the March 28 Saturday TODAY broadcast, thanking colleagues, mentors, and viewers. He described the network as “literally my happy place” but admitted the toll of travelling from Washington, D.C., to New York every week. Social media posts echoed his on-air gratitude, stressing the importance of family and his eagerness to take on something new. Hindustan Times + 3 "I’ve been away from home more than 80 nights in the last seven months, more than 220 Friday nights, 220 Fridays nights away from my family in the last seven years. So it’s a limited window before my daughters lose interest in hanging out with me. It’s happened quick. I’m eager to carve out a better balance between my personal and professional lives and to challenge myself with something new."Peter Alexander A high-profile move to MS NOW Alexander is set to anchor MS NOW’s 11 a.m. weekday programme and lead breaking news coverage, replacing Ana Cabrera. Reports suggest he will also serve as chief national correspondent and may contribute to sports coverage on affiliated networks. This marks the first transfer from NBC News to MS NOW since the networks split in 2025, underscoring the competitive realignment in cable news. Times Now + 2 From White House briefings to weekend co-host Alexander joined NBC News in 2004 after working as an anchor at its Washington affiliate, WRC. He first covered the White House between 2012 and 2014 during Barack Obama’s second term and returned to the role in 2018 to report on Donald Trump. In October 2018, he became co-host of Weekend TODAY, later teaming up with Kristen Welker in 2020, and over the years he has held high-profile assignments across flagship NBC programmes. Live Mint + 2 Shifts in U.S. broadcast journalism Alexander’s departure comes amid the rebranding of MSNBC into MS NOW under new parent company Versant, ending editorial overlap with NBC News. The split forced journalists to choose sides, with some moving to MS NOW and others staying at NBC. His move signals not only a personal career change but also the evolving competitive landscape and talent strategies in American broadcast news. Times Now + 2 6 references
